question: Can a project-side read-only adapter, without modifying the pinned Cano source, produce exactly one fixed-seed candidate with auditable successful tunnel returns, a coherent graph/spline/per-tunnel-axis bundle, and an original mesh that passes strict topology gates?
method: Run one process with PYTHONHASHSEED=0, numpy.random seed 0, Python random seed 0, reset upstream Node/Tunnel counters, and single-thread numerical environment controls. Call the pinned Cano APIs for exactly three grown tunnels and one connector, each once with its own bounded 100-trial upstream search, and reject immediately unless every return is the documented (True, Tunnel) tuple. Export a stable project-side graph.json, splines.json, per-tunnel axis.txt, upstream WorldInfo JSON, original unmodified Poisson mesh, SDF, metadata, hashes, and one full-extent diagnostic. Do not repair, filter, keep-largest-component, rerun, or count the candidate as data.
baseline: The preceding original generate_environments.py smoke emitted files but failed: its mesh had seven components and failed watertight/manifold/orientability/self-intersection gates, while 100 percent of tunnel-axis rows had cross-tunnel ID conflicts and no graph/returns/seed were exported. This adapter is compared against that preserved failure evidence and may improve observability only; it must not lower mesh gates.

user_authorization.scope: Implement and execute exactly one project-side read-only Cano audited-adapter smoke with seed 0, three requested grown tunnels, and one requested connector; no upstream modification/copy, whole-world retry, repair, batch, Isaac, LiDAR, labels, training, or M-TARE changes.
user_authorization.confirmation_reference: User message on 2026-08-10 after the exact adapter scope was presented: 继续

acceptance_criteria: E1 freeze and pip check pass; fixed source remote, commit, clean status, and native entrypoint hash match before and after; adapter, validator, runner, test, and run-spec hashes are recorded.

Exactly three grown calls and one connector call are made; every call returns the documented two-element tuple with success true and a Tunnel object. Any failed or malformed return stops the run without a whole-world retry.

graph.json contains stable node IDs/XYZ, edges, intersections, tunnel IDs/types, connected-components and cycle-rank statistics; it must be one connected component with exactly three grown tunnels, one connector, and cycle rank one.
splines.json has one finite nonempty spline per graph tunnel and every spline endpoint matches its graph endpoint within 1e-6 source units.

axis.txt uses per-tunnel accessors for tunnel-interior rows, labels all four graph tunnel IDs, gives every tunnel at least one interior row, and has zero identical interior coordinates carrying different tunnel IDs.
Upstream WorldInfo JSON, scalar FTA, SDF-to-mesh references, metadata source/seed controls, and all recorded bundle file hashes validate.

The original, unrepaired mesh is readable, nonempty, exactly one triangle component, edge manifold without boundary, vertex manifold, watertight, orientable, and not self-intersecting. No component deletion, hole filling, remeshing, or threshold relaxation is allowed.
The only preview shows all actual mesh vertices and all exported per-tunnel splines in X-Y, X-Z, and Y-Z with provenance and explicit claim limits.

Even PASS creates zero formal dataset worlds and authorizes only a later separately approved deterministic-replay specification; it does not authorize batch, Isaac/LiDAR, labels, training, or M-TARE changes.
stop_conditions: Any environment, source, import-path, tool-hash, authorization, or output-target mismatch
Any grown or connector call returns failure or an undocumented return shape
A second whole-world generation attempt would be needed
Graph, spline, per-tunnel axis, WorldInfo, metadata, file-hash, FTA, or SDF contract failure
Any strict mesh topology criterion fails
Generation exceeds 1800 seconds, validation exceeds 900 seconds, or output exceeds 3 GB
expected_evidence: Frozen command, user authorization, source/environment/tool hashes, pip check, stdout/stderr, durations, and exit codes
One temporary world_000 containing original mesh plus graph.json, splines.json, per-tunnel axis.txt, WorldInfo, generation-return audit, metadata, FTA, and SDF
Machine-readable graph/spline/axis/mesh/provenance validation and explicit PASS/FAIL claim boundary
One full-extent actual mesh plus per-tunnel spline diagnostic with provenance
Evidence SHA-256 manifest and explicit zero dataset/LiDAR/label/training counts

estimated_cost.compute: CPU-only one-candidate upstream topology, point-cloud, Poisson mesh, strict Open3D validation, and offline diagnostic; no network install, GPU, Isaac, LiDAR, or training.
